v.rationale: All three use Bus::batch with allowFailures, a finally callback, a dedicated statements queue, #[Scope] and attribute-based job config, and all test suites pass. None of them schedules pruning for job_batches or failed_jobs. impl-3 is the strongest. It puts the fan-out job inside the batch and adds the account jobs in chunks with lazyById and $batch->add, so the request stays light and memory stays flat. Because the fan-out job is part of the batch, the run reaches a final status even when the dispatcher crashes (probe confirmed). Retries with backoff and the exists() check make transient failures recover, and completion is idempotent. Its one flaw is that the failure count is off if the dispatcher itself dies. impl-2 has clean code, idempotent completion and the best real-worker tests. But its dispatcher sits outside the batch, loads all 40k models, has no timeout and no failed() handler. My probe showed a fan-out failure leaves the run 'running' forever, which breaks the core 'always reaches a final status' requirement. impl-1 keeps fan-out memory low with pluck('id') and does have a failed() fallback. However, that fallback writes completed_with_errors with failed_accounts=0 and sends no summary email (probe confirmed). It also swallows every exception through catch(Throwable)->fail() so nothing gets reported, has non-idempotent finalisation and unescaped HTML in the mail, and its tests run on the sync driver. impl-2 ranks above impl-1 on code quality and tests, even though its stuck-run bug is serious.
